free.title: FREE MOVIE NIGHT AT BRYANT PARK
free.caption:
FREE TONIGHT · BRYANT PARK

No Country for Old Men, free under the Midtown skyline tonight.

Bryant Park movie night turns the lawn into New York's biggest living room, and the pick is the Coens' Oscar-winning thriller. The lawn opens at 5PM, the film rolls at 8PM - no tickets, no RSVP, just a blanket and whoever you can round up on a Monday. Vendors sell picnic food from 4PM and there's a beer and wine bar on the grass from 5.

TIP: leave the tarp at home - plastic ground covers get turned away at the entrance.

Tag the friend who'd quote Anton Chigurh all night.

food.title: THE SECRET MENU AT LOS TACOS NO. 1
food.caption:
CHEAP EATS · CHELSEA MARKET

The best order at Los Tacos No. 1 isn't on the menu board.

Regulars at the Chelsea Market taqueria skip the board and ask for the vampiro - an open-faced tostada with a crisped cheese shell - or the quesataco, a taco wrapped in a grilled-cheese tortilla. Every one lands under $9 on the official price list, and the grilled jalapenos and onions cost nothing if you ask.

TIP: go before noon or after 2PM, and take your haul one block west to the High Line steps.

Send this to the friend who says cheap eats in New York are dead.

art.title: 6 SECRETS OF THE BROOKLYN BRIDGE
art.caption:
HIDDEN GEM · BROOKLYN BRIDGE

The Brooklyn Bridge is hiding champagne cellars, a Cold War bunker and a rooster story most New Yorkers have never heard.

The stone anchorages you walk over held wine vaults with painted frescoes, rented out until the 1930s, and a 2006 inspection turned up a forgotten fallout shelter stocked with 352,000 crackers. Emily Roebling ran the build for 11 years and crossed first in 1883 - rooster in tow. A year later P.T. Barnum marched 21 elephants across to prove it would hold.

TIP: walk it before 9AM and you'll have the boards nearly to yourself.
